claim: One parent (calculated) health check can monitor the health of up to 255 child health checks.
question: How many child health checks can one parent health check monitor?

qualifiers.condition: The console section of the health check values page says up to 256; see route53-hc-calculated-console-256

evidence.quote: One parent health check can monitor the health of up to 255 child health checks.

claim: The console page for calculated health checks says you can add up to 256 health checks to Health checks to monitor.
question: How many health checks can you add to a calculated health check in the console?

qualifiers.condition: Differs from the 255 child health checks stated on the quotas page and the determine-health page

evidence.quote: You can add up to 256 health checks to **Health checks to monitor**.

claim: A calculated health check cannot monitor other calculated health checks.
question: Can a calculated health check monitor other calculated health checks?

values.display: can't configure a calculated health check

evidence.quote: You can't configure a calculated health check to monitor the health of other calculated health checks.

claim: Route 53 counts the healthy child health checks and compares that count with the number that must be healthy for the parent health check to be healthy.
question: How does a calculated health check decide it is healthy?

values.display: number of child health checks that must be healthy

evidence.quote: Route 53 compares that number with the number of child health checks that must be healthy for the status of the parent health check to be considered healthy.

claim: If the number of healthy children you require is greater than the number of child health checks, the calculated health check is always unhealthy.
question: What happens if the healthy threshold of a calculated health check exceeds the number of children?

values.display: always considers this health check to be unhealthy

evidence.quote: If you specify a number greater than the number of health checks in **Health checks to monitor**, Route 53 always considers this health check to be unhealthy.

claim: If the number of healthy children you require is 0, the calculated health check is always healthy.
question: What happens if a calculated health check requires 0 healthy children?

values.display: always considers this health check to be healthy

evidence.quote: If you specify **0**, Route 53 always considers this health check to be healthy.

claim: A disabled child health check counts as healthy when Route 53 calculates the status of a calculated health check, unless you invert its status.
question: How does a calculated health check count a disabled child health check?

values.display: considers the disabled health check to be healthy

qualifiers.condition: Choose Invert health check status to count it as unhealthy

evidence.quote: If you disable a health check that a calculated health check is monitoring, Route 53 considers the disabled health check to be healthy as it calculates whether the calculated health check is healthy.

claim: A new health check is considered healthy until there is enough data to determine its actual status.
question: What is the status of a new health check before data arrives?

values.display: considers a new health check to be healthy

qualifiers.condition: If the status is inverted, a new health check is considered unhealthy until there is enough data

evidence.quote: Route 53 considers a new health check to be healthy until there's enough data to determine the actual status, healthy or unhealthy.

claim: HTTPS health checks do not validate SSL/TLS certificates, so a check does not fail when the certificate is invalid or expired.
question: Does an HTTPS health check fail on an expired certificate?

evidence.quote: HTTPS health checks don't validate SSL/TLS certificates, so checks don't fail if a certificate is invalid or expired.

claim: An HTTPS health check needs an endpoint that supports TLS v1.0, v1.1, or v1.2.
question: Which TLS versions must an HTTPS health check endpoint support?

evidence.quote: If you choose **HTTPS**, the endpoint must support TLS v1.0, v1.1, or v1.2.

claim: Route 53 cannot check the health of an endpoint whose IP address is in local, private, nonroutable, or multicast ranges.
question: Can a Route 53 health check monitor a private IP address?

values.display: cannot check the health of endpoints

evidence.quote: Route 53 cannot check the health of endpoints for which the IP address is in local, private, nonroutable, or multicast ranges.

claim: If you specify the health check endpoint by domain name, Route 53 uses only IPv4 to send the health checks.
question: Which IP version does a domain-name health check use?

evidence.quote: If you specify the endpoint by domain name, Route 53 uses only IPv4 to send health checks to the endpoint.

claim: New and existing customers can create up to 50 health checks for AWS endpoints within or linked to the same AWS account at no charge.
question: How many health checks for AWS endpoints are free?

qualifiers.scope: per AWS account, aggregated across all Regions
qualifiers.condition: AWS endpoints in or linked to the same account

evidence.quote: New and existing customers can create up to 50 health checks for AWS endpoints that are within or linked to the same AWS account for free.

claim: A hosted zone includes up to 10,000 records before extra record charges begin.
question: How many records does a hosted zone price include?

qualifiers.condition: Each record above 10,000 per hosted zone is charged per month

evidence.quote: A hosted zone includes up to 10,000 records.

claim: A hosted zone that is deleted within 12 hours of creation is not charged for the zone, but queries on public hosted zones are still charged.
question: How long can you keep a new hosted zone without a monthly zone charge?

qualifiers.condition: Queries on public hosted zones are still charged

evidence.quote: To allow testing, a hosted zone that is deleted within 12 hours of creation is not charged, however, any queries on public hosted zones will still incur charges at the rates below.

claim: A Route 53 Resolver endpoint requires two or more IP addresses, and each IP address corresponds with one Elastic Network Interface.
question: How many IP addresses does a Resolver endpoint need according to the pricing page?

evidence.quote: A Route 53 Resolver endpoint requires two or more IP addresses.

claim: The Route 53 Resolver (Amazon DNS server) is located at 169.254.169.253 (IPv4), fd00:ec2::253 (IPv6), and at the primary private IPv4 CIDR range of your VPC plus two.
question: At which addresses can a VPC reach the Amazon DNS server?

evidence.quote: The Route 53 Resolver is located at `169.254.169.253` (IPv4), `fd00:ec2::253` (IPv6), and at the primary private IPV4 CIDR range provisioned to your VPC plus two.
